strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Executes 8 all-reduce operations sequentially with interleaved local scaling/normalization operations, exactly as shown in the seed library. Total of 8 all-reduce dispatches with full vector payloads (W*256 elements each). Represents the straightforward no-optimization baseline with maximum dispatch count but simple correctness reasoning.

strategies.name: Fused Local Operations Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Merge all local element-wise operations (scaling by a[r]/W, division by a[r], cloning) into single fused kernels between each all-reduce pair, reducing from ~24 separate local operations to 8 fused kernels. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but fewer local-op dispatches. Trades kernel fusion complexity for reduced dispatch overhead on local operations.

strategies.name: Vectorized Coefficient Precomputation
strategies.desc: Precompute all coefficient patterns (a[r], a[r]/W, 1/a[r]) as static tensors outside the loop, then use vectorized multiply/divide operations instead of per-shard indexing loops. Maintains 8 all-reduces but replaces O(W) indexing loops with broadcast operations. Reduces local computation overhead at world_size=224 by vectorizing coefficient application.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decompose each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing local operations to execute on smaller S-sized chunks between the two phases rather than full W*S buffers. Results in 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but potentially better memory locality and opportunity for overlapping computation with reduced-size working sets.

strategies.name: Pipelined Dual-Buffer All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Use two alternating buffers to pipeline consecutive all-reduce operations, initiating all-reduce(i+1) on buffer B while completing local operations for all-reduce(i) result in buffer A. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but overlaps collective communication latency with local computation via async dispatch patterns. Reduces end-to-end latency through pipeline parallelism at cost of doubled memory footprint.
